pendingSeal.message: Certification of the boundary and topography by a Maryland licensed surveyor. The plan is complete and delivered; this is the review step that follows. The boundary shown is GIS, compiled rather than surveyed — in testing, county GIS was 4.3 ft off the surveyed line and a front setback flipped from compliant to non-compliant once corrected.

Quantify the unknown disturbance components (Building footprint, Driveway, Utility trenches, Grading, Stormwater facilities, Stockpiles, Construction access, Offsite work, Demolition, Staging areas). Until then the 5,000 sq ft determination is not defensible either way, and it decides whether sediment control and stormwater management review apply.
Read the footnotes on the dimensional table. A footnote can replace the printed value outright for a specific use or lot type.
Maryland surveyor-certified boundary and topographic survey (surveyor): GIS parcel geometry is preliminary and may be offset from surveyed boundaries. A permit submission needs certified geometry.
Recorded easements and title report (applicant): An unmapped easement can invalidate a building location after approval.
Disturbance area — Building footprint (applicant): Unquantified components keep the project above the 5,000 sq ft gate by default.
Disturbance area — Driveway (applicant): Unquantified components keep the project above the 5,000 sq ft gate by default.
Disturbance area — Utility trenches (applicant): Unquantified components keep the project above the 5,000 sq ft gate by default.
Review and seal by the professionals responsible for each subject. The platform drafts a complete plan; the seal is a human act that follows delivery. Nothing here implies county approval.

outputs.note: Jurisdiction approval is separate and not implied.
